Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and identify the current rollout artifacts. I’ll also use the required fish-control bookshelf and wake-visual inspection skills before proposing or editing the policy; their evidence requirements will shape the candidate notes and reusable lesson.

The inherited guidance already contains a long successful capture lineage, so this is not a seed-level architecture step. I’m now tracing the assigned parent and all sampled rollouts—especially the strongest fully observed capture and the most informative regression—before deciding whether the next candidate should preserve the current mechanism or add a genuinely distinct one.

The visual comparison confirms the numerical story but exposes an inherited logging mistake: the best policy has a valid two-view wake, while the response-gated regression’s oblique sheet is blank, not complete. Its top-down route and wake are nearly unchanged, so its worse mean distance is still a control-allocation regression, but it cannot support an independent 3D-wake claim. I’ll correct that reusable evidence boundary and consult the mechanism shelf for a compact next allocation that does not reopen exhausted gain-tuning paths.

The candidate will keep the best controller’s launch, carrier, course, recovery, rudder, and terminal law unchanged. The sole new mechanism is a bounded hydrodynamic-response qualifier on the already successful posterior half-cycle allocator: adverse target-signed yaw moment may recruit unused asymmetry up to the existing ceiling, while favorable moment adds nothing. This directly tests whether load feedback becomes compatible when it reallocates an established rhythmic path instead of adding a separate residual or unloading the anterior joint.

Both required provenance files are now updated, and the solver contains exactly one candidate. The durable guidance now records two important boundaries from this generation: extra recovery preview is operationally inert, and favorable-moment anterior unloading does not compose with posterior prediction. I’m checking the Julia contract, parameter schema, and candidate-only diff next; no CFD will be run.

The policy diff is confined to the allowed candidate file and adds one declared parameter before use. I’m invoking the workspace’s required lightweight check runner now; it will compare the guidance against the assigned parent, execute only the synthetic policy-contract state, and run the editable-boundary check—never CFD.

The configured checker agent could not start because its pinned model is unavailable in this account. The invocation requirement has been attempted; I’m running the exact three commands from its configuration directly so the same checks still execute, and I’ll repair and rerun any substantive failure.

The first check found a rendered-workspace metadata defect rather than a candidate defect: the same assigned guidance parent is listed twice in `README.md`, so the checker cannot resolve a unique parent. I’m removing only that duplicated listing, then rerunning the required check unchanged.

All three substantive checks pass: the notes/guidance delta is material, the candidate returns two finite accelerations under the synthetic multi-wake state, and the solver boundary contains no unauthorized edits. I’m doing a final handoff audit now; formal CFD remains deferred to EvE as required.

Produced exactly one candidate with bounded adverse-yaw-moment qualification of the existing posterior half-cycle allocator:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:29)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:288)

Recorded the bookshelf transfer and corrected the blank-oblique evidence boundary. Also removed a duplicate assigned-parent listing from `README.md` that prevented validation.

All lightweight checks pass: guidance delta, Julia policy contract, parameter schema, and solver boundary. The configured checker agent was unavailable due its pinned model, so its exact commands were executed directly. No CFD was run.
